- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 or vice versa), model lags by 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts >75% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) if sentiment is neutral or bearish; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for those days.
